requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected in a four-player game
How selected Pods are distributed and oriented at setup
Tokens initially placed in the Intruder bag
answers.answer:
1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for four players.
2. Place the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next numbered Pod in Section B, and continue alternating A/B in numerical order. All selected Pods start Locked side up.
3. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, and 1 additional Adult per player. With four players that is 7 Adults total.
answers.evidence:
1. “Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players.”
2. “Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section ‘A’, the next (in numerical order) in Section ‘B’, then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up. Return the rest to the box.”
3. “Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.” Inference: four players means 3 + 4 = 7 Adults in the bag.

requested_parts: How Objective cards are filtered and dealt
When each player chooses which Objective to keep
What happens to the rejected Objective
Whether Eggs trigger the Objective choice
answers.answer:
1. Remove from each (Corporate and Personal) Objective deck every card that requires more players than are in the game; shuffle the decks separately and deal each player one from each deck, kept hidden.
2. Each player chooses one of their two cards at the First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature appears on the board.
3. Remove the unchosen Objective from the game face down, unseen by anyone. Players may never look at other players’ removed Objectives.
4. No. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence:
1. “Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden.”
2–4. “First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others’ removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.”

requested_parts: What is discarded to pay for an Action card printed cost 2 when that card is held along with two other Action cards and two Contamination cards
Whether Contamination cards can pay the cost
How to resolve a card offering OR effects
answers.answer:
1. Discard the played Action card plus two other Action cards, for three Action cards total. The two Contamination cards are not discarded to pay.
2. Contamination cards cannot substitute for Action cards in any Action cost.
3. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one of the sections/effects.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.” “Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.” For cost 2, inference from that rule: discard the played card and 2 additional Action cards, 3 total; neither Contamination card pays.
3. “If a card has two sections separated by ‘OR,’ choose one.”

requested_parts: When Fire damage is taken by a Character who takes one Action and passes in a burning Room
Whether they can take another Action during this Player Phase
Whether they can discard cards after passing
Whether later players’ rounds cause more Fire damage to them that turn
answers.answer:
1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound at the end of their passing round, after declaring Pass.
2. No. After passing they sit out normal rounds for the rest of the Player Phase.
3. They do not take another ordinary Action or discard cards to pay for one after passing; the cited post-pass allowance is only an Interruption, and it is permitted only if they are in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action.
4. No. Later players’ rounds do not give that Character further Fire wounds that turn.
answers.evidence:
1, 4. “Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players’ rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.” “Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.”
2. “I. Player Phase: … rounds of 2 Actions (or 1 Action + pass, or pass) clockwise until all players pass — after passing you sit out normal rounds for the rest of the Phase (Interruption remains permitted).”
3. Inference from the Player Phase rule that passing sits the Character out of normal rounds: they have no further ordinary Action to pay for or discard cards for. The summary specifies the exception: “Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere.”

requested_parts: What happens when entering an empty unexplored Room: tile and Item Counter
How the Exploration effect resolves
When the Noise roll occurs and where the resulting token/marker goes
How Silence alters the Noise roll
How Danger alters the Noise roll
How an already occupied destination alters the Noise roll
answers.answer:
1. Flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal its Exploration token, and set the Item Counter to the number shown on the token (except the Nest and Room Covered With Slime, which have no Item count).
2. Resolve the Exploration effect and then remove that token from the game. Silence or Danger replaces the ordinary Movement Noise roll; resolve that result without rolling again.
3. If the result is not Silence or Danger and the destination is empty, roll Noise. On a 1–4 put a Noise marker in the correspondingly numbered Corridor connected to the entered Room (including Technical Corridors where applicable); if that Corridor already has a marker, resolve an Encounter instead. A Noise roll result of Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or, if none are eligible, places markers in every connected Corridor lacking one. Silence places no marker.
4. Silence means no Movement Noise roll and nothing happens, unless the Character has Slime, in which case Silence resolves as Danger.
5. Danger means no Movement Noise roll: move all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the entered Room. If no eligible Intruders exist, place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor without one.
6. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not roll Movement Noise. (A Silence/Danger Exploration result is resolved as stated and itself does not call for a Noise roll.)
answers.evidence:
1–2. “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.” “Item Counter: the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token’s number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.”
3–5. “Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” “Danger: if there is an Intruder in a neighboring Room (and it is not in Combat with any Character), move it into this Room — all eligible Intruders move. If there are no Intruders in neighboring Rooms (or they are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one (counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance).” “Silence: nothing happens; no marker. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve ‘Danger’ instead.”
6. “Remember: never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement cost and what it replaces
When Careful Movement is forbidden
Whether a Closed Door can be crossed
Whether a miniature can stop in a Corridor
answers.answer:
1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. After entering the destination, instead of rolling Noise, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to that Room. It also replaces an automatic Silence or Danger Exploration result with that chosen Noise placement.
2. It is forbidden in Combat and if every Corridor connected to the destination already has a Noise marker.
3. No. Normal Movement restrictions apply, and a Closed Door blocks passage.
4. No. Characters and Intruders may occupy Rooms only and may never stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence:
1–3. “Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement.”
4. “Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.”

requested_parts: Encounter sequence caused by rolling a number for a Corridor that already has Noise
What happens to Noise
Where the drawn token goes
How Surprise Attack is determined
Whether Contamination cards count in that comparison
answers.answer:
1. Since that Corridor already has a Noise marker, resolve an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers in every Corridor connected to the Room (including connected Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance); draw one Intruder token; place its matching miniature if it is not Blank; then compare the drawn token’s number with the triggering player’s hand.
2. The connected Noise markers are discarded at the start of the Encounter. If the bag draw is Blank, instead put a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to the Room; the Encounter ends without an Intruder appearing, and return the Blank token to the bag.
3. Keep a drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank is returned to the bag after its procedure.
4. If the triggering player has fewer cards than the number on the non-Blank token, the appearing Intruder makes a Surprise Attack against that Character; equal or more means no Surprise Attack.
5. Yes. Both Action and Contamination cards in the triggering player’s hand count.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” “Resolve: 1. Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance). 2. Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure. 3. Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. 4. Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.”
3–5. “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” The quoted Encounter rule explicitly includes Contamination in the comparison and gives the non-Blank token destination.

requested_parts: How Danger resolves with several eligible neighboring Intruders
What Danger does when no Intruders are eligible
Whether an Intruder moving into your Room counts as an Encounter
How Slime affects Silence
answers.answer:
1. All eligible Intruders in neighboring Rooms move into the Room; eligibility excludes an Intruder in Combat with any Character.
2. If there are no eligible neighboring Intruders (including when neighboring Intruders are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that does not already have one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.
3. No. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; they are simply in Combat.
4. While the Character has Slime, every Silence result on a Noise roll or Exploration token resolves as Danger.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.”
3. “An Encounter is any instance of an Intruder appearing (via an Intruder-bag draw) in a Room where a Character is present. Some Event cards (e.g., Hatching) and Intruder Attack cards can also trigger Encounters. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat).”
4. “while on your board, every ‘Silence’ result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes ‘Danger.’”

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank during a Blank Encounter draw
Whether an Adult is added in an Encounter with Blank
What happens to Blank during bag development
answers.answer:
1. For a Blank drawn during an Encounter, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to that Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without a miniature appearing. The opening Encounter step has already discarded all Noise markers from all connected Corridors.
2. Add an Adult token to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag; if no Adult is available, nothing is added.
3. During bag development, Blank adds 1 Adult token to the bag if one is available, then returns to the bag; if none is available, no Adult is added.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” The Encounter sequence also says: “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance).”
3. “Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.”

requested_parts: Where two Intruders attempting together to cross one Closed Door end
What happens to the Door
Whether it can later close
Whether a Noise-triggered appearance is blocked by the Closed Door
answers.answer:
1. Both Intruders stay in the Room they were trying to leave; neither crosses the Closed Door.
2. The Intruders destroy the Door.
3. A Destroyed Door allows movement through it and only the Plasma Torch Item can close it again.
4. No. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put).”
3–4. “Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it.” “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”

requested_parts: What happens to an injured Intruder miniature when it moves into Technical Corridors
What happens to its Injury markers and token
What happens to Noise in Technical Corridors
Whether Characters or Door tokens normally use those Corridors
answers.answer:
1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed from the board.
2. Discard all Injury markers from it and return its token to the Intruder bag.
3. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains there; the Intruder movement does not remove it.
4. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except via the Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card or the Technical Corridor Plans Item card. Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence:
1–3. “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.”
4. “Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic’s ‘Technical Corridors’ Action card and the ‘Technical Corridor Plans’ Item card).” “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Shoot Action costs and target location
Melee Action costs and target location
Contamination handling for Melee
What happens on a miss for each Action
What a two-hit die result does for each Action
answers.answer:
1. Shoot costs one Action card and one Ammo. Choose a Weapon in your Hand with at least one Ammo and an Intruder in your Room, discard one Ammo, then roll. A Shoot miss deals no Injury and causes no Wound to the shooter.
2. Melee costs one Action card and targets an Intruder in your Room.
3. Before rolling Melee, draw one Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile.
4. A Melee miss deals no Injury and inflicts one Serious Wound on the attacker.
5. A double-hit result deals 2 Injuries in Shoot (before any Weapon modifier), but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence:
1. “Shoot (cost 1): requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo. (1) Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room; (2) discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon card; (3) roll the Combat die.” “A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter.”
2–4. “Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die. Results mirror Shooting with two changes: any miss also inflicts 1 Serious Wound on your Character, and the 2-Injury result deals only 1 Injury (in melee, rolls of 2 Hits are treated as 1 Hit).” “A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.”
5. “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers | 1 Injury to any Intruder type.”

requested_parts: How a Larva’s death is checked
How an Adult’s death is checked
How a Queen’s death is checked
When a Carcass is placed
What happens if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow
answers.answer:
1. A Larva dies from 1 Injury. Its miniature is removed and no Carcass is placed.
2. For an Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value with the Adult’s current total Injuries: blood less than or equal to Injuries means it dies; higher means it remains alive. On death remove its miniature and place a Carcass in the Room.
3. For a Queen, draw two Intruder Attack cards and sum their blood values; sum less than or equal to current total Injuries means death, otherwise it remains alive. On death, place a Carcass in the Room.
4. Carcasses are placed when Creepers, Adults, Breeders or Queens die; not for Larvae.
5. If either card drawn for the Queen shows a Retreat arrow in its blood icon, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result: draw an Event card, move the Queen through the Corridor numbered in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence:
1–4. “Intruder Injuries and death: after any Injuries, put that many Injury markers on the Intruder’s base and check its Injury Effect. Compare current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.” The table states: “Larva | 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass”; “Adult | Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; and “Queen | Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.”
5. “During an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card’s blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card’s Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: When Escape attacks occur and their order for two Intruders
Who is targeted by the Escape attacks
What happens if the Character dies
What follows if the Character survives into an empty unexplored destination
answers.answer:
1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger types: Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva.
2. Each Escape attack targets the escaper.
3. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to Escape from.
4. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring Room. Since it is unexplored, explore it normally; because it is empty, perform the Movement Noise roll unless the Exploration result or a movement effect replaces/cancels it.
answers.evidence:
1–3. “To leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” “A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.”
4. The Escape rule above explicitly requires normal exploration and Noise “if the destination is empty.” Movement rule: “if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box.” “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.”

requested_parts: How the target is chosen when several Characters are present
How ties are broken
How a non-Larva hit is determined
What changes for a Larva attack
Where the Larva attack’s Contamination card is placed
answers.answer:
1. The Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand.
2. On a tie, choose the Character with the First Player token, or the next player in turn order.
3. For an Intruder other than a Larva, draw one Intruder Attack card; a matching attacking-Intruder symbol means resolve the card’s effect (a hit), and a nonmatching symbol means the attack misses.
4. A Larva draws no Intruder Attack card. It moves from the board to the target’s Character board and the target gains one Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing Larva stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this does not automatically kill them.
5. Put the gained Contamination card on top of the target’s Action discard pile.
answers.evidence:
1–3. “Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order). A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.” “Larva exception: draw no Attack card; use Infest below. For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder’s type, resolve the card’s effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks.”
4. “A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target’s Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).”
5. “When a Character ‘gets a Contamination card,’ draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether dressing one of three Serious Wounds prevents death from a further Light Wound
What happens when a Character with two Light Wounds receives a third
What Heal removes
Where the dead Character’s Corpse and Heavy Objects go
answers.answer:
1. No. A Character with three Serious Wounds dies upon any additional Wound, and dressing only ignores a wound’s effect; it still counts toward the three-wound limit.
2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound.
3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.
4. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room as a Character Corpse Object and drop all their Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence:
1. “A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious).” “Dress a Serious Wound: flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds.”
2. “On a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.”
3–4. “Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.” “Death: … Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.”

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Canteen/Shower scan and remove
How Canteen/Shower handle an Infected card with and without an existing Larva
Which cards Surgery scans and removes
How Surgery handles a Larva
Surgery costs and turn/hand consequences
answers.answer:
1. Canteen and Shower scan all Contamination cards in the Character’s hand. Remove scanned non-Infected cards from the game. An Infected card is kept.
2. If there was no Larva on the board before the scan, an Infected result places a Larva on the Character board. If a Larva was already present, the Character dies and a Creeper is placed in the Room.
3. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard pile, and removes all Infected cards from the game.
4. Surgery also removes a Larva from the Character board if present.
5. Surgery is a Room Action (cost 2 Action cards); after scanning and removal the Character suffers 1 Light Wound and automatically passes. Shuffle all their cards, including their entire hand and remaining Contamination cards, into their Action deck; the hand stays empty until the next turn. Surgery does not give a new Contamination card.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “For the optional Canteen/Shower hand scan, the complete outcome is below. Larva status means before this Room scan.” The table states: “Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result”; “Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board”; and “Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.”
3–5. “Surgery — Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” “Room Actions cost 2 Action cards.” The surgery sentence lists scan/removal, Larva removal, wound, pass, shuffle and empty hand; it grants no new Contamination card.

requested_parts: How Shoot/Melee, Grenades, Molotovs, and Fire destroy uncarried Eggs
Which Melee penalties are waived against Eggs
When Noise is rolled after Egg destruction attempts
When the Nest is destroyed
answers.answer:
1. Shoot or Melee destroys one Egg per Injury. A Grenade destroys two Eggs. A Molotov destroys one Egg immediately, and its Fire marker can destroy further Eggs during later Fire Damage steps. A Fire marker normally destroys one uncarried Egg per Event Phase Fire Damage step; with Vulnerability to Fire, the Nest’s Egg pool loses two per such step.
2. For Egg Melee, a successful attack still draws one Contamination card, but a miss causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The summary leaves unresolved how to reconcile the normal pre-roll draw with that missed-attack exception; it specifies no refund or alternative draw timing.
3. Roll Noise after every individual Shoot, Melee, Grenade, or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, even on a miss. If a Grenade/Molotov targets the Nest remotely, roll Noise in your own Room.
4. When no Eggs remain on the Intruder board (whether carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed and marked with one Injury marker.
answers.evidence:
1. “Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below.” “Grenade | Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there.” “Molotov Cocktail | Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps.” “Fire marker | Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest’s Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).”
2. “A successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified.”
3. “After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).”
4. “When no Eggs remain (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.”

requested_parts: What permits entering a Pod and what prevents entry
What must be resolved before boarding
How many Characters and Heavy Objects fit
Options and consequences when waiting in a Pod
answers.answer:
1. To enter, perform the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action for 2 Action cards. The Pod in that Section must be Unlocked and have a free Character space. Entry is forbidden while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. A Noise roll that makes an Intruder appear in or reach the Section also makes entry fail.
2. Roll Noise before entry; if an Intruder appears or is present in the Section, the attempt fails.
3. A Pod holds two Characters. Heavy Objects do not take Character spaces.
4. Choosing to wait makes you pass the current turn; you remain treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose to wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and play a full round of two Actions. If an Intruder appears in the Section, every Character in any Pod there immediately returns to the Section Room. requested_parts: Order of endgame checks
Outcome with two Damaged Engines
Outcome of a non-Earth destination for hibernating Characters, including Quarantine Objective at Mars
Contamination procedure for an infected survivor or one with a Larva
Whether launched Pod passengers undergo Contamination checks
answers.answer:
1. Resolve Engines, then Coordinates, then Contamination, then Objectives.
2. Two Damaged Engines make the ship explode; everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. Launched Pod passengers are already away.
3. A non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters while the ship is not destroyed; Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars.
4. If at least one Contamination card is Infected, or the Character already has a Larva, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand, and discard together into a new Action deck and draw the top four. Any Contamination card among those four kills the Character, whether Infected or not; four Action cards and no Contamination means they survive the check. A Character with a Larva skips the initial scan but still does this shuffle and draw.
5. Yes. The Contamination check applies to every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers.
